text: First, stcsanalysis data analysis packages loaded: path STCS data-cut assigned stcsat_dir (eg: stcsat_dir = "path//stcs/data-cut/folder/csv/"), data can loaded follows:

First, select identifiers stcs$patientdisease. , var_available() function displays variables might merged, given -key data. key (eg: patientkey, diseasekey patientkey, date), list variable can join current data displayed. Note variables stcs$stop proposed patientkey, date unique identifier stcs$stop variable name available dataset. However, date represent type events (diagnostic VS stop), hence, merging using two dates make sense. variables chosen, add_var() used include data. patientkey available data-set, variables stcs$patient might added/join current data-set. , simply add enrollment_age: variable-name appears several tables, name table must specified using = argument.

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: is_truemissing() function used detect Missing type Missing can set NA using truemissing_to_na(). set NA: NOTE: STCS contains Missing type logical data-type.
code: v_chr <- c("data", "Missing", "again data") v_dbl <- c(1, 2, -9999, -9998) v_dt <- c(as.Date("1700-01-01"), as.Date("2020-12-25"))  is_truemissing(v_chr) #> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE is_truemissing(v_dbl) #> [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE is_truemissing(v_dt) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE truemissing_to_na(v_chr) #> [1] "data"       NA           "again data" truemissing_to_na(v_dbl) #> [1]     1     2    NA -9998 truemissing_to_na(v_dt) #> [1] NA           "2020-12-25"

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: paste_valuecomment() function used handle “value - comment” pairs: instance, can used infection-level data-set keeping infection-site information:
code: paste_valuecomment(c("value1", "value2"), c(NA, "comment2")) #> [1] "value1 | value2:comment2" stcs$infectionsite |>    slice(1:100) |>    summarise(     infsite_n = n(),     aggr_infiste = paste_valuecomment(infsite, comment),     .by = diseasekey) |>    arrange(desc(infsite_n)) |>    slice(0) #> # A tibble: 0 × 3 #> # ℹ 3 variables: diseasekey <chr>, infsite_n <int>, aggr_infiste <chr>

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: stcs$medicationtreatment contains interval data. Depending relevant categorization, might overlap merging first analysis step. following example, periods induction drugs merged patients. useful compute instance number days induction first months:
code: # warning: this processing does not consider inaccuracy of date. stcs$medicationtreatment |>   filter(drug_category == "drug_ind") |>   # NA stop-date are considered as ongoing treatment   mutate(medication_startdate = replace_na(medication_stopdate, stcs$admin$extraction_date)) |>   # Missing/NA stop and stop date are considered as data-entry error   filter(!is.na(truemissing_to_na(medication_startdate))) |>   filter(!is_truemissing(medication_stopdate)) |>   filter(medication_stopdate >= medication_startdate) |>   reframe(     merge_intervals(medication_startdate, medication_stopdate, .lag = 1),     .by = patientkey   ) |>   slice(0) #> # A tibble: 0 × 3 #> # ℹ 3 variables: patientkey <chr>, x0 <date>, x1 <date>

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: actual date assessment assdate recorded STCS, however aligning date expected date protocol often useful. assessment baseline, M6, Y1, Y2, …, one can use closest_value() aligning effective time protocol time. can done follow: NOTE: might several assessments pp_days events (eg: transplantation, death) trigger assessment.
code: stcs$patientlongitudinal |>    left_join(     summarise(stcs$organ,                tpxdate = min(tpxdate),               .by = patientkey),     by = "patientkey",     relationship = "many-to-one"   ) |>    select(patientkey, patlongkey, assdate, tpxdate) |>    mutate(eff_days = as.integer(assdate -tpxdate),          pp_days = closest_value(eff_days,                                   target = round(c(0, 186, 365.25*c(1:25))))) |>    slice(0) #> # A tibble: 0 × 6 #> # ℹ 6 variables: patientkey <chr>, patlongkey <chr>, assdate <date>, #> #   tpxdate <date>, eff_days <int>, pp_days <dbl>

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: time--(first)-event variables derived using base::pmin() (time) together .pmin_chr() (event). simple example using 3 types event:
code: # time of event  eventA <- c(1, 2, 3, 2) eventB <- c(2, 1.5, NA, 2) eventC <- c(NA, NA, 2, 3)  # time of first event  pmin(eventA, eventA, eventC, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 1 2 2 2 # Which event come first?  ## In case of ties, display all. which.pmin_chr(A = eventA, B = eventB, C = eventC, ties = "collapse") #> [1] "A"     "B"     "C"     "A | B" ## In case of ties, choose according to the order in the function. which.pmin_chr(A = eventA, B = eventB, C = eventC, ties = "first") #> [1] "A" "B" "C" "A" which.pmin_chr(B = eventB, A = eventA, C = eventC, ties = "first") #> [1] "A" "B" "C" "B"

title: Introduction to stcsanalysis
text: Combining previous functions, Kaplan-Meier estimator patient survival derived follow:
code: tb_km <-    # Use the tailored "survival" table   patsurv |>    select(patientkey, enrollment_date, first_dropoutdate,           last_assdate, last_consent_withdrawal_date, deathdate,          extraction_date) |>    # Only select patients with consent (last known value)   add_var(stcs, "last_consent_status") |>    filter(last_consent_status == "Present") |>    # Last-assessment should not censored the terminal event   mutate(last_assdate = replace(last_assdate, !is.na(deathdate), NA)) |>    # Compute time to death, censoring for dropout, last-assessment,    # consent withdrawal and STCS data extraction date.   mutate(     event_date = pmin(       deathdate, first_dropoutdate, last_assdate,        last_consent_withdrawal_date, extraction_date,         na.rm = TRUE),     event_chr = which.pmin_chr(       death = deathdate, cens = first_dropoutdate, cens = last_assdate,       cens = last_consent_withdrawal_date, cens = extraction_date,       ties = "first")) |>    mutate(event_01 = as.integer(event_chr == "death"),          event_days = as.integer(event_date -enrollment_date))  km <- survfit(Surv(event_days, event_01) ~ 1, data = tb_km) plot(km)
